w10_P4_001458: A 146 000 g cart is accelerated on a test rail. The rail is 20 m long. The acceleration, in m/s², is obtained from a gauge reading by subtracting 25 and then adding 23, where the gauge reading is the larger root of x² - 9x + 14 = 0. Express the force needed in kN.
w10_P4_001463: A 189 000 g crate is accelerated on a dock at a rate, in m/s², equal to the greatest common divisor of 131 and 316. The dock is 15 m long. The motor also overcomes 26 N of friction, while a slope supplies 22 N of the total. Express the force the motor supplies in kN.
w10_P4_001464: A 108 kg robot is accelerated across a factory floor at a rate, in m/s², equal to the area under the curve y = 4x² + 4x from x = 0 to x = 1. A slope supplies 19 N of the force needed, and a cable adds 3 N of drag. The factory runs 6 identical robots per line and 9 lines. What total force, in N, must the drives supply?
w10_P4_001470: A coach wants the combined energy figure, in kilojoules, of 2 identical sleds, each with 21 J added by a push to its energy of motion. Each sled has a mass of 35 kg. Each sled's speed, in m/s, equals the area under the curve y = 2x² + 3x from x = 1 to x = 4. What is the combined energy figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001471: A depot wants the total force, in newtons, for 10 lines of 7 identical 183 kg carts, less 23 N recovered by a shared regenerative rail. The carts are 2 m long. The acceleration, in m/s², is the greatest common divisor of 210 and 150. What is the total force, in N?
w10_P4_001475: A 187 kg cart is accelerated on a test rail. The controller sets the acceleration, in m/s², by taking the greatest common divisor of 140 and 30, doubling it, multiplying by 4, and subtracting 9. The cart is driven by a linear motor. Express the force needed in kN.
w10_P4_001481: A lab wants a final figure, in kilonewtons: 11 kN from a clamp, plus 6 kN from a spring, plus the force to accelerate a 5 kg cart, expressed in kilonewtons. The cart's acceleration, in m/s², equals the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 1·x from x = 1 to x = 2. The cart runs on an air track. What is the final figure, in kN?
w10_P4_001488: A depot wants the total force, in kilonewtons, for 6 identical lines. Each line's figure is the force for 9 identical 56 000 g carts, expressed in kilonewtons, plus 2 kN for the line's drive. The carts are 1.4 m long. The acceleration, in m/s², equals the number of ways to choose 2 wheels from 6. What is the total force, in kN?
w10_P4_001492: A 169 kg cart is accelerated at a rate, in m/s², equal to 4 times the sum of 7 and 10. The cart is 1.8 m long. The depot runs 5 carts per line; each line's force is expressed in kilonewtons, and there are 10 lines. What is the total force, in kN?
w10_P4_001496: A coach wants the total energy figure, in kilojoules, of 9 teams of 3 identical riders. Each rider's figure is the energy of motion of a 60 kg rider-and-bike, expressed in kilojoules, plus 17 kJ from a battery boost. The track is 250 m long. The speed, in m/s, is the slope of the curve y = 1·x³ + 2x² at x = 3. What is the total energy figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001500: A 19 kg cart on a lab bench moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to the larger root of x² - 6x + 5 = 0. It loses 27 J of its energy of motion to friction. The remainder is expressed in kilojoules, and a heater adds 30 kJ to the cart's energy account. What is the final energy figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001505: A 49 000 g model kart moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to the slope of the curve y = 3x³ + 1·x² at x = 1. A club runs 4 identical karts per heat and 4 heats per session, with the session total expressed in kilojoules. The club holds 4 sessions. What is the total energy of motion, in kJ?
w10_P4_001508: A safety officer wants the total energy figure, in kilojoules, for 3 identical sleds, each expressed in kilojoules. Each sled's figure is its energy of motion plus 20 J from a push. Each sled has a mass of 58 kg. Its speed, in m/s, is found by doubling the sum of 7 and 3 and then subtracting 9. What is the total energy figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001514: A 15 000 g cart moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to the rate at which the slope of the curve y = 1·x³ - 1·x² is itself changing at x = 4. Its energy of motion is expressed in kilojoules. A battery adds 22 kJ to the cart's energy account, the total is multiplied by 5 for 5 identical carts, and a heater adds 6 kJ. What is the final energy figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001517: A coach wants the final energy figure, in kilojoules, of a sled after a 5 J push, before which 18 J was added by a ramp, and before that 12 J was lost to friction from its energy of motion. The sled has a mass of 49 000 g and is 1.2 m long. Its speed, in m/s, equals the number of ways to choose 2 runners from 11. What is the final energy figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001522: A lab wants the total energy figure, in kilojoules, for 2 identical carts. Each cart's figure is its energy of motion, expressed in kilojoules, plus 23 kJ from a heater, plus 20 kJ from a battery. Each cart has a mass of 29 kg. Its speed, in m/s, equals the number of ways to choose 4 sensors from 7. What is the total energy figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001524: A club wants the net energy balance, in kilojoules, of a launcher's battery: 30 kJ drawn by the launcher's heater is subtracted from the net delivered energy, expressed in kilojoules. The net delivered energy is the combined energy of motion of 6 identical 5 000 g projectiles, less 15 J lost to friction. Each projectile's speed, in m/s, is the greatest common divisor of 129 and 368. What is the net energy balance, in kJ?
w10_P4_001530: A depot wants the rated force, in kilonewtons: a 16 kN reserve is added after 21 kN supplied by a gravity assist is subtracted from the force for 7 identical 163 000 g carts, expressed in kilonewtons. The carts are 2.2 m long. The acceleration, in m/s², equals the rate at which the slope of the curve y = 3x³ - 5x² is itself changing at x = 3. What is the rated force, in kN?
w10_P4_001532: A coach wants the total energy figure, in joules, of 8 identical sleds plus 4 J stored in a starting gate. Each sled's figure is its energy of motion plus 23 J from a push plus 2 J from a nudge. Each sled has a mass of 39 000 g. Its speed, in m/s, is the larger root of x² - 7x + 10 = 0. What is the total energy figure, in J?
w10_P4_001534: A depot wants the total force, in kilonewtons, for 7 sites, each with 10 identical carts, with each cart's force stated in kilonewtons. Each cart's force is what accelerates its 48 000 g mass plus 29 N of friction. The carts are 1.6 m long. The acceleration, in m/s², equals the number of ways to choose 4 wheels from 7. What is the total force, in kN?
w10_P4_001540: A depot wants the force, in kilonewtons, to accelerate a 38 kg cart. The acceleration, in m/s², is found by taking the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 7x from x = 0 to x = 1, multiplying by 3, adding 22, and subtracting 15. The cart runs on a 10 m rail. What is the force, in kN?
w10_P4_001549: A lab wants the net energy balance, in kilojoules, over 6 identical runs. Each run's balance is the cart's energy of motion, expressed in kilojoules, plus 7 kJ from a charger, minus 9 kJ drawn by a heater. The cart has a mass of 57 kg. Its speed, in m/s, is the smaller root of x² - 8x + 7 = 0. What is the net energy balance, in kJ?
w10_P4_001553: A depot wants the total force, in newtons, for 6 identical lines. Each line's figure is the force for 9 identical 172 kg carts, less 13 N recovered by a regenerative unit, less 7 N supplied by a slope. The carts are 2 m long. The acceleration, in m/s², is the greatest common divisor of 261 and 17. What is the total force, in N?
w10_P4_001558: A coach wants the total energy of motion, in joules, of 9 identical sleds, each having gained 17 J from a push after losing 14 J to friction. Each sled has a mass of 14 kg and is 1.1 m long. Its speed, in m/s, equals the number of ways to choose 2 runners from 10. What is the total energy of motion, in J?
w10_P4_001563: A dock wants the net force, in kilonewtons, for 2 identical 107 kg carts, less 9 N supplied by a slope. The carts' acceleration, in m/s², is found by multiplying the sum of 9 and 6 by 3 and subtracting 15. The carts share one winch. What is the net force, in kN?
